"Double The Money" has gone close to two months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $100,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

If you play "Double The Money" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2415.headline: Good news: no big claims

2416.body:
"Loaded with $2,000s" has 1,366 of 3,372 top prizes left and is past the halfway point of its run. About two-thirds of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

If you play "Loaded with $2,000s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2416.headline: How much has sold

2419.body:
A $2,777 top prize on "Bronze 7s" was claimed last week. The game started with four top prizes and has one top prize left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "Bronze 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2419.headline: The top prize list got shorter

2420.body:
One of Silver 7s's top prizes was claimed last week. A player in Virginia won $177,777. The game started with three top prizes and now has two top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

The numbers for "Silver 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2420.headline: Top prize count went down

2421.body:
A $577,777 top prize on "Gold 7s" was claimed in the latest numbers. The game started with three top prizes and has one top prize left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Everything here about "Gold 7s" comes from official Virginia lottery numbers, current through October 27.
2421.headline: A top prize was just claimed

2422.body:
Platinum 7s's prizes make it a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of the prize money still unclaimed, about two-thirds is in wins under $2,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

Every line of Platinum 7s's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.

2426.body:
